transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I’m here because I’m having a real problem on job sites now. I’m a construction manager, so I’m around scaffolds and roof edges and upper platforms all the time, or I’m supposed to be. And lately every time I get near one, even if I can clearly see the guardrails are there and I know the setup is supposed to be safe, my head just starts telling me I’m about to go over.

It’s weird because I know how these things are built, you know? I’ve been around sites forever, and I can look at something and tell it’s secured. I mean, I’ve had crews argue with me about rail placement and tie-offs and all that—sorry, that’s probably not the point. The point is, I get near the edge or the scaffold, and it’s like my brain doesn’t believe what my eyes are seeing. It just says, “You’re going over.”
Is this fear or sensation limited to being on job sites and near heights, or have you noticed similar feelings of anxiety in other situations as well?

Mostly it’s the heights, yeah—job sites, scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms. That’s where it hits me. I mean, I can be standing there looking right at the guardrails, knowing they’re installed right, and still my head just goes, “You’re about to go over.”

It’s not like I’m walking around anxious everywhere, if that’s what you mean. It’s when I have to get near those edges or up on something. Which is ridiculous in my line of work, because half my day is supposed to be checking that stuff.
When you feel that fear near heights, do you find yourself avoiding those situations or doing anything specific to cope with it?

Yeah… I have been avoiding it, pretty badly. I’ll kind of make it sound like a scheduling thing, but I’ve been handing off the height inspections to my foremen a lot more than I should. Or I’ll move a meeting that should be up on the deck down to ground level, like, “Oh, it’s easier for everyone,” but really it’s because I don’t want to go up there.

And if I absolutely have to go up, I make someone stay right next to me. Usually I rush through whatever I’m supposed to check and get back down as fast as I can. I’m scared the whole time, even if I’m trying to act normal.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or panic in situations that weren’t related to heights, like in crowded places, driving, or being alone?

I don’t think so… not like out of nowhere. I mean, driving in traffic is annoying, sure, and crowded places can get on my nerves—my wife drags me to those big warehouse stores on Saturdays and it’s like everyone forgets how to steer a cart—but I wouldn’t call that panic.

The thing that really flips the switch is the height stuff. If I’m on the ground, or in a truck, or just by myself somewhere, I’m not usually getting that sudden “oh no” feeling. It’s when I’m up near an edge or thinking I have to go up there.
Do you ever start feeling anxious or panicky even before you get to a height situation—like if you know you’ll have to go up on a scaffold later in the day?

Yeah, I mean… it’s mostly tied to knowing I’m going to be up there. If I look at the schedule and see I’ve got to check a scaffold or get near a roof edge or one of those upper platforms, I start thinking about it before I even get there.

And it’s stupid because I know the rails are there. I can see them, I know how they’re supposed to be installed—I’ve been doing this long enough to know when something’s safe. But my head just starts telling me, “You’re going to go over,” like it doesn’t matter what I know.

It’s like when you’re packing for a job and you can’t find the one tool you need, and the whole morning gets stuck on that one thing—except it’s not the tool, it’s the thought of standing near that edge. Then by the time I’m actually up there, I’m already worked up.
Do you start feeling anxious or panicky hours or even the night before you have to go up on a scaffold or near a roof edge?

Yeah… it can start before, for sure. I’ll see it on the plan or remember, “Tomorrow I’ve got to get up near that roof edge,” and then my head kind of latches onto it.

It’s the same thing every time now—scaffold, roof edge, upper platform—doesn’t matter if I can see the rails are there or I know, logically, the setup is supposed to be safe. I’ve been around construction long enough to know the difference between safe and stupid, you know? But my brain just goes, “You’re going over.” And then I’m thinking about that instead of, I don’t know, ordering materials or whether the concrete guys are going to show up on time.
Do you find yourself having trouble sleeping the night before you have to go up on a scaffold or near a roof edge because your mind keeps going back to the thought of being up there?

I’m not sure I could say that, exactly. I mean, some nights I sleep lousy anyway—job stuff, calls, schedules, my kid leaving lights on all over the house, whatever—but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s specifically the night before being up on a scaffold.

I do know once I start thinking about the height part it can kind of stick in my head, but as far as lying there all night because of it… I don’t know. I’d have to think about that more.

When you're near a scaffold or roof edge and start feeling anxious, does the fear ever reach a peak within minutes, where your heart races, you feel short of breath, or feel like you're going to lose control?

Yeah, it comes on pretty fast. Like the second I step onto those temporary stairs, or even if I’m just walking toward an open upper floor, my chest tightens up and my hands get all wet.

And then I start thinking, “Just move, just take the next step,” but my legs feel like they’re going to lock up before I can make myself do it. It’s ridiculous because I’m there to do a job, not stand there like some apprentice on his first day—though honestly some apprentices are calmer than me up there. But yeah, it hits within minutes, sometimes almost right away.
Do you ever feel anxious or worried when you’re not near heights or even thinking about them—like when you’re at home or doing something completely unrelated?

I don’t know… I mean, I get worried about normal stuff, sure. Bills, work schedules, whether somebody ordered the wrong size beam and now everybody’s acting like it’s my fault—stuff like that.

But if you mean that same kind of feeling out of nowhere, when I’m just sitting at home watching TV or something, I haven’t really noticed it. It’s hard to separate sometimes, because my head’s always got some job thing running in the background, you know? But I don’t think it’s like the height feeling unless something reminds me of that.
Do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worried even when you’re not near heights or thinking about having to go up somewhere?

Not really… I mean, I’m anxious about plenty of regular life stuff, like everybody is. Work’s always got something—subs not showing up, inspectors changing their minds, my phone buzzing while I’m trying to eat dinner. My wife says I bring the job home with me, which is probably true.

But if you mean that specific worried feeling about going up high when I’m nowhere near it and not thinking about it, I don’t know that I’d say that happens. It’s more when something puts it in front of me, or I know I’ve got to deal with it. Otherwise it’s just… normal stress, I guess.
Even though you know the guardrails are secure and the setup is safe, do you constantly worry that you might fall whenever you're in a high place?

Yeah… pretty much. I can look right at the guardrail and know, logically, it’s there. I mean, I’m the guy who’s supposed to know whether the setup is right, half the time I’m the one telling other people to tie off or stop leaning over like idiots.

But when I’m up there—scaffold, roof edge, an upper platform—my head just goes, you’re going over. Like it doesn’t matter that the rails are in place or that the guys checked it. I start picturing it, or not even picturing it exactly, just this strong feeling that one wrong step and I’m gone.

Which is annoying, because I’ve been on sites forever. I used to give people grief for being nervous up high. Now I’m standing there staring at a perfectly safe edge like it’s going to pull me over.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about falling or worrying about heights even when you're in a completely safe place, like at home or in your car?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. Like, if I’m at home, I’m usually thinking about whatever’s going on with the job or trying to get through dinner without my phone going off. In the car, I’m mostly annoyed at traffic or some guy hauling a trailer with half his load strapped wrong—drives me nuts.

I mean, maybe if something reminds me of it, like seeing a crew up on a roof while I’m driving, then my mind goes there for a second. But just sitting somewhere safe and suddenly worrying I’m going to fall? I haven’t really noticed that. It’s more when I’m actually dealing with heights, or I know I’m about to.
